_about: Propellant gauging, loading spread, low level cutoff and running dry. Every value has its source. 'My arithmetic' marks a number computed from published values. Percent values are of the tank's full load. Page references follow the authors' research notes, copied into results/issue-72/sources.md.

load_spread_sd.source: Root mean square of loaded-against-predicted deviations over nine Saturn V stage flights, 18 values (S-IC, S-II, S-IVB on AS-504, AS-505 and AS-506; my arithmetic): MPR-SAT-FE-69-4 Table 5-2 and 6-3, MPR-SAT-FE-69-7 Table 5-2 and p. 6-10, MPR-SAT-FE-69-9 Table 5-2 and p. 6-9. Range -0.24% to +0.50%. The gauging model uses 0.26% from the S-IVB rows; the two agree.

capacitance.source: Continuous capacitance probes (S-II and S-IVB PU systems, Centaur). Error 1 sigma = sd_floor + sd_per_fill x fill, of full load: about 0.30% at ignition and 0.05% near empty. Fit by eye to the PU-indicated against best-estimate values: S-IVB AS-504 to AS-506, liftoff -0.01% to -0.42%, first cutoff -0.07% to -0.56%, second or third cutoff -0.09% to +0.03% (MPR-SAT-FE-69-4 Table 7-12, -69-7 Table 7-3, -69-9 Table 7-3); S-II at ground ignition -0.37% to +0.30% (Table 6-3, 6-2, 6-2); Centaur LH2 left at LOX depletion under 0.15% of load over nine flights and probes within 0.2% in 1 g tests (NASA TN D-4848, abstract and p. 12 to 13). Needs settled liquid: Shuttle OMS gauging updates only while an engine burns and has no probe data for the first 15 s of a burn (USA006500 Rev. A, OMS Workbook, p. 33 to 35). Probes do not reach the tank bottom; Centaur valves are nulled 15 s to 25 s before cutoff (TN D-4848 p. 14; TM X-1989 p. 60), which is about 3% to 5% of a Centaur load (my arithmetic), so the probe is blind below 3% of load. Not used: the S-II open-loop PU-probe readings at the valve step on AS-505 and AS-506 (+2.4% and +4.7% of load), which the reports do not explain and which the transient model's notes flag as unchecked.

point_sensors.source: Discrete level sensors with flowmeter integration between them (S-IC and S-II). At a sensor the level is known to about 0.03% of load: the S-II point-sensor mass is the best estimate the reports use, and the S-IC level sensors agree with the reconstruction within 0.07% to 0.12% (MPR-SAT-FE-69-4 Table 5-2 and Sec. 6.5). Between sensors the reading is flowmeter integration, whose error against the best estimate is 0.29% (LOX) and 0.66% (LH2) of load (MPR-SAT-FE-69-4 Table 6-3); here 0.5% of the mass used since the last sensor. The sensor heights are an assumption (the reports give the number of sensors, not their heights).

pvt.source: Pressure-volume-temperature gauging of the helium pressurant; works in zero g. Shuttle RCS gaging module design analysis, 3 sigma of maximum deliverable propellant: fuel 2.9%, 3.3%, 3.9% and oxidizer 3.3%, 4.2%, 5.4% at 100%, 50% and 0% remaining (Duhon, Design Note 1.4-2-9, NASA-CR-150966, NTRS 19760025152, Table I, PDF p. 11); divided by 3 here. The larger Shuttle OMS is worse, 8.0% to 9.5% 3 sigma (Design Note 1.4-2-10, NTRS 19770003201, Table II, PDF p. 11). NASA Glenn ground tests: under 2% of tank volume in steady state (NASA/TP-2014-218083).

default_gauge.source: The gauge of the Saturn S-II and S-IVB, Centaur and the Shuttle OMS.

low_level_cutoff.source: Depletion sensors stop the engines before a pump runs dry: S-IC LOX level sensors start the outboard cutoff timer, S-II cuts off when 2 of 5 sensors in one tank go dry, S-IVB depletion sensors, Shuttle ECO sensors (MSFC-MAN-503 p. 63, 105, 123; NTRS 20110015703). The trip level is usable propellant left above the unusable residual the stage mass already carries (vehicle.py, 0.5% of capacity): 0.15% of load, from S-II LOX residuals at cutoff of 665 kg to 816 kg out of about 372 t (0.18% to 0.22%, MPR-SAT-FE-69-4 p. 117, -69-7 p. 6-10, -69-9 p. 6-9) and the AS-504 S-IC early trip that left 2,561 kg usable LOX (0.17%, -69-4 Sec. 5.1). Every flown stage of these vehicles carries them, so a stage has them unless its design sets low_level_cutoff false.

pressure_fed.source: No pump. Pressurant gas follows the last liquid into the chamber and the engine stops; nothing turns, so nothing overspeeds.

electric_pump.source: The motor controller limits speed, but a pump that ran without liquid has lost its liquid-cooled bearings (Proton Breeze M, Yamal 402, 2012: pump ran without normal liquid cooling and the bearing failed; ILS statement).

expander.source: No combustion in the turbine drive, so no hot gas when a propellant runs out, but gas flow overspeeds the pumps: RL10 tests avoided gas flow 'to avoid damage due to overspeed from gas flow' (NASA CR-174914, p. 32 to 36).

gas_generator.source: Fuel-rich gas generator. When oxidizer runs out first the gas generator goes leaner and colder and the engine stops: the Atlas sustainer was cut off by LOX depletion on every flight, with the PU valve driven oxidizer-rich-stop 'to make sure LOX ran out first' (NASA TM X-1989, AC-16, p. 59). When fuel runs out first the gas generator burns oxidizer-rich and the turbine burns.

staged_fuel.source: SSME: low-level cutoff exists 'to preclude the catastrophic consequences of an LO2 depletion shutdown' (HPOTP overspeed; Worlund et al., NASA CP-2342 Part 2, p. 26 to 27). The HPOTP may 'unload and overspeed causing a catastrophic shutdown' if the prevalves close late (JSC-19041, SSME Overview, p. 97).

staged_ox.source: As staged_fuel: a staged-combustion turbopump unloads and overspeeds when its liquid runs out.

full_flow.source: As staged_fuel; both turbopumps run on preburner gas.

flight_performance_reserve.source: Saturn V AS-503: FPR 2,390 lb (1,084 kg), the root-sum-square of 3 sigma vehicle dispersions at TLI, about 1% of the S-IVB load; FPR plus the flight geometry reserve gives 99.865% assurance (MSFC-MAN-503, p. 2-2). Atlas-Centaur Surveyor: 3 sigma reserve of 175 lb to 255 lb (JPL TR 32-1265, Table VIII-3). Not a simulator rule: a team carries it by loading more than its burns need.
